meta.title: Flipkart smartphone buyers during Big Billion Day

prompt: Estimate the number of customers purchasing smartphones from Flipkart during the Big Billion Day Diwali sale.

clarifications.answer: Only internet users can shop online; the book uses ~40% internet penetration on a 1.4 billion population, so ~0.56 billion in focus.
Split the focus population urban/rural 30:70, then by income, applying a likelihood-to-buy-online to each cell (summing to ~0.19 billion).
Flipkart holds ~40% of online electronics; a person replaces a phone about once every 3 years.
About 50% of Flipkart's annual smartphone sales land in the Big Billion Day / Diwali window. Answer in crore buyers.

common_traps: Applying Flipkart's share to the whole population instead of to likely online smartphone buyers.
Forgetting the replacement cycle, so the stock of potential buyers is never converted to annual buyers.
Ignoring the Diwali concentration and reporting the whole-year Flipkart figure.

anchors.1: Guesses a number with no penetration-to-buyers-to-share chain.
anchors.3: Builds an online-buyer estimate but omits the replacement cycle or the Diwali concentration.
anchors.5: Chains internet penetration, purchase likelihood, Flipkart share, replacement cycle and the Diwali share.

anchors.1: Treats the whole population as identical online shoppers.
anchors.3: Segments urban/rural but with a single purchase likelihood.
anchors.5: Segments by locality and income with distinct online-purchase likelihoods per cell.

anchors.1: Loses the billion/crore conversions; lands orders of magnitude off.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a slip, landing just outside 0.8-2 crore.
anchors.5: Carries the share, replacement and Diwali fractions cleanly, landing near 1.3 crore.

anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Cross-checks that ~1.3 crore Diwali buyers is a believable fraction of ~7.6 crore Flipkart-preferring online shoppers.
